name: Howard Starr
life: “I still remember meeting a pupil's parent in hospital visiting hours.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Howard by a small Friday habit. Howard starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I checked her records at night and thought she was a new arrival despite our daughters sharing a classroom.
appearance: Howard has a dark undercut with a longer wave on top, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Howard starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Howard has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To recognize the patient before classifying arrival history.
family: June Kent is Howard’s half-sibling. Howard asks what the birthday guest would like this year. June remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, June says, “I bought the umbrella secondhand. I've found the aunt who made the dress and she wants to tell me about it.”
connections: Anton Roman. Two people at the hospital work out what other waiting patients actually need to be told.
